districtFact: Tucson Unified School District serves students in Tucson and Pima County. Its school-year calendar is especially useful for families because it combines weekly one-hour early-release Wednesdays, parent-teacher conference half days by grade band, grading and planning no-school days, Rodeo Break, and a May graduation and last-day window.

about.title: About Tucson Unified School District
about.content: Tucson Unified School District, commonly called TUSD, serves students in Tucson, Arizona. The district's one-page calendar lists the first and last student days, weekly Wednesday early release, parent-teacher conference half days, grading and planning days when students do not attend, professional learning days, Rodeo Break, fall break, winter break, spring break, graduation days, and staff reporting dates.

about.title: District Calendar and School-Level Schedules
about.content: This page covers districtwide TUSD calendar dates from the official English calendar PDFs. Families should still check their school for bell schedules, transportation, athletics, testing windows, graduation ceremony times, magnet or program calendars, and campus-specific announcements.

planningTips.title: Tucson Unified Calendar Notes
content: TUSD releases students one hour early every Wednesday, so weekly pickup and after-school arrangements can differ from the rest of the week.
Parent-teacher conference dates are half days, and the K–8 conference windows do not always match the grades 9–12 conference dates.
Grading and planning days are no-school days for students, not normal attendance days.
Rodeo Break is a distinct February no-school break on the TUSD calendar and should not be grouped with spring break.

districtFaqs.q: Does Tucson Unified release students early every Wednesday?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. Students are released one hour early every Wednesday. Families should confirm exact dismissal times with their school.

districtFaqs.q: Are TUSD parent-teacher conference dates half-days?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. TUSD parent-teacher conference dates are half-days. K–8 students have more conference half-days than students in grades 9–12.

districtFaqs.q: What is Rodeo Break on the TUSD calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Rodeo Break is a February no-school break listed on the Tucson Unified calendar. It is separate from winter break and spring break.

districtFaqs.q: Where should families verify Tucson Unified calendar updates?
districtFaqs.a: Use the official Tucson Unified School District calendar page and school announcements for final confirmation. MySchoolDates is an independent reference and is not affiliated with TUSD.
